newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SEES MIDDLESBROUGH IN EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SEES MIDDLESBROUGH IN EUROPE.

text.p: Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli, who has in the past suggested he wants to return to Italy from England, said on Friday that he was happy at Middlesbrough and willing to stay there.
"I feel lighter now," the former Juventus star told the Turin daily La Stampa newspaper in an interview under the headline "Ravanelli: I'll win two cups and stay."
"I have a four-year contract with Middlesbrough, where I am really at home," he said.

Ravanelli said he was hopeful that the club, anchored to the bottom of the premier league after being docked three points, would avoid relegation after picking up their form and also qualify for Europe by winning a domestic trophy.
"I have really missed the European Wednesdays but I could rediscover them with Middlesbrough," he said.
"If we win the League Cup we'll go into the UEFA Cup and if we win the F.A. Cup, there's the Cup Winners' Cup.
"This club has never won anything. If Ravanelli brings them a cup and also the title of top scorer it will be as if I had won another European Cup," the player said.
Middlesbrough reached the first major cup final in their 121-year history on Wednesday when they overcame Stockport County in the League Cup semifinals.
They are also through to the semifinals of the F.A. Cup.
Ravanelli said life in England was quieter than in Italy and he felt less pressure as a result.
"This calm is attractive to Italian players, watch how many arrive next year and big, unexpected names," he said.
